assumedContext: No primary filing retrievable; findings rest on the Q2 2026 results release and financial press.

findings.claim: Q2 2026 produced record adjusted EBITDA of USD 1.767bn, up more than 30% year on year from USD 1.35bn. Operationally the quarter was strong.
findings.label: FACT

findings.claim: And revenue missed badly: USD 4.02bn against a consensus of USD 5.73bn, down 5.5% year on year. Revenue fell 5.5% while adjusted EBITDA rose 31%, in the same quarter.
findings.label: FACT

findings.claim: That divergence is not a contradiction, it is the structure of the business. Vistra's reported revenue and GAAP net income swing on unrealised mark-to-market movements in its hedge book — Q2 net income was only USD 305m against USD 1.767bn of adjusted EBITDA. Revenue and earnings per share are poor instruments for this company; adjusted EBITDA and adjusted free cash flow before growth are the real ones, which is why this dossier excludes a price-earnings multiple.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE

findings.claim: Full-year 2026 guidance was reaffirmed at USD 6.8-7.6bn of adjusted EBITDA, with management stating it is comfortable delivering at or above the midpoint, alongside adjusted free cash flow before growth of USD 3.925-4.725bn.
findings.label: MANAGEMENT GUIDANCE
findings.unit: USD m FY2026E adjusted EBITDA midpoint

findings.claim: The cash generation is the strongest fact in this dossier. Adjusted free cash flow before growth of roughly USD 4.3bn at the midpoint against a market capitalisation of roughly USD 47.5bn is a yield of about 9.1%. Nothing else in this batch generates cash at that rate relative to price.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE

findings.claim: The exposure that broke the share price is disclosed and specific: the 2028 book is only about 72% hedged. Roughly 28% of 2028 is open to a forward curve management has described as softening.
findings.label: FACT
findings.source: Vistra hedging disclosure and analyst coverage

findings.claim: Demand classification: the roughly 3.8 GW under 20-year AWS and Meta PPAs is [Existing Contracted] at the best quality in this batch; the hedged portion of the near-term merchant book is [Existing Contracted] but short-dated; the 433 MW of contracted uprates is [Approved / Committed Pipeline] with a customer already attached; the unhedged ~28% of 2028 and beyond is merchant exposure earning no contracted weight; and any assumption that further large tranches of the 27 GW gas fleet contract with hyperscalers at premium prices is [Speculative Demand] earning zero base-case weight.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE

findings.claim: The monetisation structure is therefore barbelled and the thesis describes only one end of it. A small, superb, twenty-year contracted nuclear book at one end; a large, cyclical, ERCOT-concentrated merchant fleet at the other. The equity is a claim on both, and the second is bigger.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE

risks.text: About 28% of the 2028 book is unhedged into a forward curve management has described as softening.
Guidance is on free cash flow BEFORE growth capital expenditure, so the headline 9.1% yield overstates what reaches shareholders.
GAAP revenue and net income are distorted by hedge marks, so the reported figures are a poor guide and the adjusted figures cannot be independently checked here.
Any further large hyperscaler contracting of the gas fleet is speculative and earns zero base-case weight.

conclusions: Operationally Q2 was excellent: record adjusted EBITDA of USD 1.767bn, up more than 30%, with FY2026 guidance reaffirmed at USD 6.8-7.6bn and management comfortable at or above the midpoint.

Revenue missed consensus by 30% in the same quarter — USD 4.02bn against USD 5.73bn expected. That is hedge accounting rather than business deterioration, and it is why this dossier uses adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow and excludes a price-earnings multiple entirely.

The cash generation is the strongest fact here. Adjusted free cash flow before growth of roughly USD 4.3bn against a USD 47.5bn market capitalisation is about a 9.1% yield — the highest in this batch by a wide margin.
The exposure that broke the share price is specific and disclosed: only about 72% of the 2028 book is hedged, leaving roughly 28% open to a curve management has called softer.

The structure is barbelled and the thesis describes one end. A small, superb, twenty-year contracted nuclear book at one end; a large, cyclical, ERCOT-concentrated merchant fleet at the other. The equity is a claim on both, and the second is bigger.
thesisImpact: Phase 3 establishes that the valuation must rest on adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow rather than on reported earnings, and that the base case must mark the unhedged book to a softening curve rather than to the record just delivered. It also establishes the strongest counter-argument to a negative view: a 9.1% cash yield is a lot to be paid while waiting.
